articles.title: Aston Villa and Chelsea still enemies despite transfer pipeline, insists Emery
articles.summary: Martínez and Jackson latest duo to move between clubs. Goretzka and Suzuki could make debuts against Arsenal. Unai Emery has said Aston Villa and Chelsea are enemies rather than friends, insisting the clubs want to “kill” each other despite regularly doing business in recent years.
body: Emiliano Martínez became the latest player to move between the teams, after Chelsea paid £117m to sign Morgan Rogers from Villa this summer. Nicolas Jackson, who could become Villa’s record signing after joining in a deal worth up to £65m, and Alejandro Garnacho both joined Villa from Chelsea in this window, the latter on a loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy.

The fee for Rogers was a record for a British player, while the clubs agreed a £7.5m deal for Martínez, who for a second successive season expressed his desire to leave Villa Park. Austin MacPhee, the set-piece coach who was among a trio of Emery’s core staff to leave this summer, also joined Chelsea from Villa.

Last year, Villa signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and in 2024 paid £37.5m to sign Ian Maatsen permanently from the London club. Carney Chukwuemeka and Omari Kellyman, now of Borussia Dortmund and Strasbourg respectively, moved in the opposite direction in previous seasons, in 2022 and 2024 respectively.
Emery played down the notion that Villa enjoy good relations with Chelsea. “Good relations? The relationship is only through the deals – for money, for other players,” he said.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta ‘begging’ Premier League to expand 20-man matchday squads
articles.summary: Arsenal manager says dropping players ‘affects wellbeing’ Serie A allows 25-player matchday squads and La Liga 23. Arsenal have asked the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads, with Mikel Arteta saying the current system is detrimental to player welfare.
body: Arsenal have competed on multiple fronts in recent seasons. Last year, as well as winning the Premier League, they reached the finals of the Champions League and Carabao Cup, as well as the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. With pressure increasing on the football calendar and players facing more matches, Arteta sees no reason why English teams should operate with smaller squads than those from other European leagues.

“I’ve been begging the Premier League if we can extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing, because I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have,” Arteta said, as he prepares for the champions’ trip to Aston Villa on Monday night. “But these are the rules, and within the rules we have to play. We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

articles.summary: Promoted Málaga slump to 4-0 defeat at the Bernabéu. Como defeat Napoli; Jones makes Inter debut in win. Real Madrid maintained their perfect start to the season in La Liga with a comfortable 4-0 home ⁠win over promoted Málaga on Sunday, scoring three times inside 30 minutes before adding a late…
body: Jude Bellingham’s brilliant solo opener, an own ⁠goal by the Málaga goalkeeper, ⁠Alfonso Herrero, and ​a sharp Kylian Mbappé volley in effect settled the contest before half-time, with the substitute Arda Guler wrapping up the victory in added time at ⁠the Bernabéu.
The win lifted Madrid to nine points from three matches, two clear of Atlético Madrid and Alavés. Barcelona, fourth on six points with a ⁠game in hand, host Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute ‌with a superb burst through the middle, collecting a loose ball near the edge of the area, gliding past three defenders and firing low beneath Herrero. They ​doubled their lead seven minutes later after Herrero could only palm out Mbappé’s effort. Bellingham headed the rebound back towards goal and, as Herrero and a teammate collided while trying to clear, the ball ended up in the net.

articles.title: All-time great Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin stacked LA Rams
articles.summary: Los Angeles were already Super Bowl favorites. Defensive tackle was 10-time Pro Bowler with Rams. 35-year-old aiming to win second Super Bowl in LA. Aaron Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, is coming out of retirement to rejoin his only professional team, the Los Angeles…
body: During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32.

The 35-year-old returns to a stacked Rams roster who were already betting favorites to win the Super Bowl this season. The team includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback and the reigning defensive player of the year, Myles Garrett, who Los Angeles acquired in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June.
ESPN reports that Donald will earn $20m in his one-year deal, which could rise to $30m with bonuses.

Rumors had circulated that Donald would return after the trade for Garrett. Rams head coach Sean McVay had undergone a “very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played” to see if he was still able to play in the NFL. McVay said the 10-time Pro Bowler had been “outstanding” during a workout with the Rams this summer.

articles.title: Carles Gil joins elite club with New England Revolution masterclass
articles.summary: By Dylan Butler. Carles Gil put on a clinic to lead the New England Revolution to a 3-1 win over Columbus Crew at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field. And in the process, the former Landon Donovan MLS MVP placed himself in some rarefied air on Sunday.
body: With his 1g/2a, the Revs captain increased his career total to 152 goal contributions (57g/95a), making him the 20th player in MLS history to reach 150-plus goal contributions.
Gil picked up an assist on Matt Polster 's 32nd-minute equalizer that canceled out Brais Méndez 's opening goal for Columbus.
The Spanish playmaker then slipped a ball in for Dor Turgeman to increase the Revs lead to 2-1 just before halftime.
Gil put the icing on the cake with a clipped golazo in the 79th minute, his eighth goal of the season.

articles.title: ESPN insider predicts huge MVP breakthrough for Luka Doncic
articles.summary: ESPN insider predicts huge MVP breakthrough for Luka Doncic originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Luka Doncic has already built the résumé of an NBA Most Valuable Player. The one thing missing is the trophy.
body: ESPN insider Tim MacMahon believes the 2026-27 season could finally change that.

Doncic enters the season as the unquestioned centerpiece of the Los Angeles Lakers, and expectations surrounding the franchise have shifted following significant offseason changes. MacMahon believes that combination could create a compelling MVP narrative if Doncic keeps Los Angeles among the Western Conference’s top teams.
“I think it’s pretty well set up for Luka to potentially win his first,” MacMahon said. “And a narrative where the expectations for the Lakers are as low as they’ve been since LeBron arrived.”
Last season, he averaged 33.5 points, 8.3 assists and 7.7 rebounds while appearing in 64 games. Los Angeles finished 53-29, but Doncic ultimately placed fourth in MVP voting.

articles.title: Joey Votto says Reds lack mentors for Elly De La Cruz, Sal Stewart
articles.summary: NBC's Sunday Night Baseball broadcast for the Cincinnati Reds - Chicago Cubs series finale included analysis from former Reds great Joey Votto about what Cincinnati needs for young stars Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart. "The more I succeeded, the greedier I got," Votto explained.
body: "Is that Scott Rolen for you?" analyst and former Reds pitcher Jeff Brantley asked.

"Definitely," Votto replied. "Definitely. I also played with Junior. Ken Griffey Jr. The great Ken Griffey Jr. I played with several veteran players that were clear stars that helped mentor me. Some of them in the prime of their career."
Votto added that Reds catcher Tyler Stephenson remaining in Cincinnati at the trade deadline did help.

"Cincinnati is among the smallest cities in all of Major League Baseball," Votto added. "But we're also the first Major League team. The city has charm. It has history. We have the Big Red Machine. We have icons. Some of the greatest players in the history of the sport wore our uniform. Cincinnati needs to be a centerpiece place in Major League Baseball. And Tyler felt that. He knows it's a special place.... And he's happy to stay."

articles.title: Britain's Samuel causes huge shock as Boulter wins but Norrie bows out at US Open
articles.summary: Britain's Toby Samuel won his maiden Grand Slam match after an impressive straight-sets victory while Katie Boulter also won through, but Cameron Norrie lost on the opening day of the US Open.
body: Samuel, who came through three rounds of qualifying, stunned former top 20 player Tomas Machac 6-2 6-3 6-2 in just 90 minutes with a superb display of serving and groundstroke hitting.
"I'm so tired - but otherwise I'm so happy to have got the job done there," said Samuel, who was ranked 683 in the world this time last year.
"I played a great match - I'm just so thankful to everyone that has supported me to this moment, and hopefully I can carry on into next week.

"The first two sets I wasn't missing any balls. In the third, he came out a bit stronger - I had a little dip in the first few games, but I came out of it quickly. I'm just going to try and do exactly what I did today in the next match."

articles.title: Scheffler holds off Hovland to break more records with FedExCup win
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler came through a final-round tussle with Viktor Hovland to cap off another PGA Tour season in style with FedExCup glory at the Tour Championship.
body: Scheffler overturned a three-shot deficit during an eventful Sunday at East Lake Golf Club, where he mixed six birdies with two bogeys to post a four-under 66 and pull clear of the field.

The world No 1 finished on 16 under and three strokes clear of Hovland, who led at various points on the final day, with Scheffler claiming the $10m first prize and joining Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods as the only multiple FedExCup champions.
Hovland posted a final-round 72 to finish second ahead of Ryan Gerard, with Rory McIlroy recovering from three bogeys in his first five holes to post a one-under 69 and share fourth spot.

McIlroy was joined on 11 under by Ludvig Åberg, Chris Gotterup, Russell Henley, Jacob Bridgeman, first-round leader Min Woo Lee and England's Alex Fitzpatrick, with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood a further shot behind.
